spec_notes: The spec (docs/shiploop/spec.md) does not contradict the request. Decisions it marks as its own ("Default adopted"): trimming and refusing control characters, 400/404/409 codes, raw field five blank for null. Decisions in ordinary requirement lines without a marker: a no-op on a resolved or closed ticket is 409 (implied by "resolved or closed tickets yield 409"), unassignment sends no message, the outbox per-assignment key, and "Combine recognized filters by intersection", which changes the service's existing status+priority behaviour (the base answered the union) without saying it is a change, though it matches the request and docs/api.md. Pinned choices a correct product need not share: exactly field five with a blank in raw mode, no message on unassignment. Silent on transitions and the assignee, filter matching rules, show, POST/PATCH with assignee, and release notes. R-4 lists specific things to keep (Node 22, no deps, npm start, version 1 snapshots) rather than "everything keeps working".
tests_notes: TC-1 to TC-5 each cover many behaviours: TC-2 bundles ten malformed bodies, a title check, the 64 limit, open/in_progress/resolved/closed rules and 404; TC-3 bundles the name filter, case sensitivity, the empty filter, status+priority intersection and cursor paging; TC-5 bundles legacy load, persistence, CLI table/raw/show and the weekly report. Tied to internals: TC-4 calls service.worker.tick() twice and counts sent events exactly (4); TC-5 matches the table by spacing (/T-0002.*  -  /) and the "-" marker. Would fail on another correct build: TC-1 requires trimming "  Ada Lovelace  "; TC-2 requires 400 for an unknown extra field and 409 for a no-op on resolved/closed (200 unchanged is also acceptable); TC-4 requires no notification on unassignment; TC-5 requires the raw fifth column (raw unchanged is acceptable) and "-" in the table. test/helpers.js was edited (host 127.0.0.1); the existing test files themselves are unchanged and pass with the original helper too.
maintainer: Notification keys are built from the audit sequence number (ticket.assigned:<id>:<seq>), so the outbox deduplication silently depends on audit numbering, and changing either breaks the "every assignment notifies" guarantee without an obvious link. matchesFilters is shared by the API and the CLI and now intersects; the persistence loader reuses the HTTP validator ticketAssignee, so tightening API name rules would make existing data files refuse to load (and it already trims stored names silently on load).
